title: SSC CPO English
summary: SSC CPO Paper I English past questions from 16 shifts, 2024 to 2025, five a day. Questions SSC asked again and the question types it keeps asking come first, ranked together by how often they were asked, then every other question. A set of linked items counts as one question.
note: Repeats are counted across the 16 SSC CPO Paper I shifts, June 2024 and December 2025, including questions SSC reprinted word for word. SSC writes fresh questions for almost every shift; a word or idiom it asks again is a repeat, and a grammar rule it keeps testing is a type. Vocabulary, idioms, cloze and comprehension passages are each their own fact, so they are not grouped into types. Groups were found by a chapter-by-chapter reading (scripts/homework/REVIEW_BRIEF_SSC.md) and checked in the main session. Questions marked defective are left out.

groups.label: Inversion after a negative or restrictive opener (At no point, Barely): auxiliary before subject
Simple past verb in a past-tense narrative sentence (told, began)
Voice change of a question (yes/no or wh-question)
Voice change with said/supposed/presumed/required/found + infinitive or that-clause
Voice change in a continuous tense (is/was being + past participle)
Voice change in a perfect or perfect continuous tense (has/had been)
Voice change with a modal (will, could have, ought to)
Voice change in simple present or simple past
Indirect to direct speech: undo the backshift of a reported statement (would to will, had to have)
Indirect to direct speech of a reported conditional (if, unless, were, had, only if)
Direct to indirect speech: tense backshift of a reported statement
Direct to indirect speech: reporting a question (asked if/whether/wh-, statement order)
Reporting a wish or prayer (If only, I wish, May ...)
Reporting an order or request (told/requested + to-infinitive)
Article or no article before an abstract noun (hope, foresight, law, consensus)
Passage set with grammar-identification questions (voice, clause role, tense) and a word meaning
Skating on thin ice / on thin ice: meaning or use
Under the weather: feeling unwell
Take it with a grain of salt: accept with doubt
Beat around the bush: avoid the main point
Bread and butter: means of livelihood
Four lettered sentences (A-D) of a short narrative moment: order them
Five long numbered sentences on a historical or scientific topic: order by chronology and reference
Four numbered steps of a workplace process (draft, review, feedback, adjust): order them in time
Four numbered sentences: general opening statement, then follow This/However/Consequently links
Adjective or adverb: an adverb modifies a verb or participle, an adjective follows a linking verb (seriously injured, ate greedily, tasted sweet)
After be/have, the main verb needs -ing or a participle (will be arranging, is cleaning, not 'is knows', 'was provide')
Verb number with a collective or plural-sense noun (the committee works, the people have)
Verb agrees with the head noun, not a nearer noun or clause (the seeds of character are, a fall in the price has)
Keep a past-time sentence in the past (dreamed that I was, a deer ran, an idea struck)
No 'will' in an if or when clause about the future (If his father gives, When my father comes)
Comparative with 'than any (other)' (greater than any other, taller than any other boy)
Article 'an' before a vowel sound (an igloo, an international, an environment)
'The' before a unique proper name (the Himalayas, the Ganga, the Statue of Liberty)
Base verb after a modal or 'to' (will teach, wanted to visit, expected to reach)
Wrong form of the same root word (celebration for celebrated, believe for belief, signification for significance)
Missing article before a singular countable noun (buy a horse, introduced a mechanism)
Unreal condition takes 'were' (If I were you, If I were very rich)
Third conditional: Had + past participle, main clause 'would have' + past participle
Base verb after suggest/advise that (suggested that the firm discontinue, advised that he take rest)
'Prefer' takes 'to', not 'than' (prefer tea to coffee)
'Whom' after a preposition (to whom, in whom)
Double comparative (more wiser, comparatively better)
Synonym of 'condemn' (denounce, censure)
One word for a lover of mankind who gives to the needy: philanthropist / philanthropy
Meaning of "propitiate" (asked as antonym and as synonym)
Meaning of "intransigence" (asked as synonym and as antonym)
Meaning of "gregarious" (asked as one-word substitution and as synonym)
